construct: Biallelic CSF2RA loss disrupts GM-CSF receptor signaling required for normal alveolar macrophage maturation and surfactant catabolism, causing hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis with intra-alveolar surfactant accumulation.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A child with crazy-paving imaging, milky PAS-positive lavage, negative GM-CSF autoantibodies, and biallelic CSF2RA variants has hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis due to defective GM-CSF-dependent alveolar macrophage surfactant clearance.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Failure of surfactant synthesis by type II pneumocytes could also cause severe lung disease, but it would not explain CSF2RA receptor deficiency or the PAP mechanism of accumulated surfactant from failed macrophage catabolism. PCD, CFTR dysfunction, and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency affect distinct airway or protease pathways.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The gene clue and anti-GM-CSF-negative PAP phenotype specifically identify hereditary receptor-signaling failure, making macrophage surfactant clearance the unique cellular defect.
